meta.title: The Small Bear and the Sledge

paragraphs: Lily drew a cartoon with six pictures for Explorers' Blog. Leo helped her with the colors. They used white, green, brown, and red crayons. Teacher Kim read the cartoon first, and she smiled. Lily wrote one line under each picture. Here is the story.

Picture one. A small bear wanted to join the Big Sledge Competition. He loved to go fast on a hill. He had a little old sledge, and it was quite slow. Picture two. The other animals had new sledges. The rabbit's sledge was red, and the cat's sledge was blue. The small bear was unhappy, and he asked, "Can anyone help me?"

Picture three. The competition began on a white hill. The sun was warm, and the snow was soft. A rabbit, a cat, and a mouse sat on their sledges. The small bear sat on his old sledge and waited. Picture four. "Go!" said the rabbit, and all the sledges went down the snow. The rabbit was first, and the cat was second. The small bear was the last one.

Picture five. Then he saw the mouse in the snow. Her sledge was broken, and she was alone in the snow. The small bear stopped and said, "Come with me!" "Thank you!" said the mouse. There was enough room on his sledge for two. Picture six. They went down the hill together, and they laughed. At the bottom, all the animals clapped for them. Now the small bear was happy. The rabbit and the cat were glad, too.

Leo looked at the last picture and said, "I like the mouse." "Why did the bear stop?" asked Mia. "A race is not only about going fast," said Lily. "A friend is more important." "I agree," said Mia, "and I love the last picture." Leo put the cartoon on the blog with a big green flag.
text.summary: Lily draws a cartoon of six pictures for Explorers' Blog. A small bear with an old sledge is unhappy before a sledge competition, but he stops to help a mouse, and they go down the hill together.
